title: Barred Spiral Galaxy NGC 6217
caption: Barred spiral galaxy NGC 6217, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: NGC 6217 · about 60 million light-years away (source figure)
credit: NASA, ESA, and the Hubble SM4 ERO Team

recognition.text: NASA Hubble image release (STScI). No published audience rating.

story: This Hubble image of the barred spiral galaxy NGC 6217 was the first astronomical picture made with the Advanced Camera for Surveys after its repair. Its distance is 60 million light-years, and it sits in the far northern sky.

Astronauts restored the camera during the STS-125 servicing mission in May 2009, which upgraded the Hubble Space Telescope, and the galaxy was photographed in June and July as part of the camera's first tests and calibration. On the same mission, astronauts installed two new instruments, Wide Field Camera 3 and the Cosmic Origins Spectrograph, and repaired the Advanced Camera for Surveys and the Space Telescope Imaging Spectrograph at the circuit board level.

Before the servicing mission, only three unique instrument channels still worked. Afterward there were 13, and NASA declared Hubble a fully rejuvenated observatory, more sensitive and able to finish observations in a fraction of the time older instruments needed. A barred spiral like NGC 6217 has a bar-shaped band of stars across its center, with spiral arms extending from it.

understand.summary: Hubble's ACS took this image. NASA shows F814W and the hydrogen-alpha filter F658N in red, F625W in green and F435W in blue.
understand.eye: The exposures total 3.0 hours, gathering far more light than the eye could from a galaxy this far away.

explore: At the time, NASA expected the upgraded telescope to study everything from Kuiper Belt objects at the edge of the solar system to the atmospheres of planets around other stars, and to make the deepest near-infrared image of the universe yet attempted.
